item.title: Watch the full series of Arkanaut on Warhammer TV now
item.description: All three episodes of the Warhammer Age of Sigmar animation are available to stream.
item.content:encoded:
The third and final instalment of the new Warhammer Age of Sigmar animation Arkanaut is live now, and available to watch on Warhammer TV. Warhammer+ subscribers can stream it at their leisure. If you’re not signed up yet, check out this trailer to see what you’re missing:

Can't see this video?

This video is hosted on a third party website, which may be using cookies. To see it, you need to accept cookies by clicking on the button below. You can change your preferences at any time by clicking Cookie Settings at the bottom of any Warhammer Community page.

Warning – if you’ve not watched the first two episodes yet, there are spoilers ahead!

Episode 3 opens with the remaining Arkanauts at the mercy of a new adversary – a Helsmith of the Fallen Ancestor Hashut. This first animated view of the Bullfather’s followers gives us a glimpse at just how divergent this culture is from their Kharadron cousins, and specifically, their perspective on power and technology.

The Kharadron Overlords and the Helsmiths of Hashut have a common lineage in the Khazalid empire of old – a culture that still endures relatively unchanged as the Khazalite Holds. The technology of their ancestors revolved around runes and the innate resonant magic of stone.

Both the Kharadron and the Helsmiths have since abandoned this technology. The Kharadron as there are not many rocks kicking about in the sky, and the Helsmiths as “harmony with nature” is not really how they roll.

Kharadron technology revolves around the use of a lighter-than-air material called Aether-gold, also called “the Breath of Grungni”. This powers not only their airships, but also their suits, weapons, and cities. In fact, without it, the entire Kharadron civilisation would quite literally come crashing to the ground. So the Kharadron dedicate much of their efforts to the finding and extraction of this valuable resource.

The Helsmiths have harnessed an altogether more dangerous material. Their technology runs on the distilled soul-essence of captured and processed daemons. As you might imagine, this is a volatile and unpredictable energy source, but incredibly powerful.

The Helsmiths believe that they are untainted by the use of this power, and that they have the willpower and fortitude to endure contact with this Chaotic essence. Their malevolent demeanor, sprouting tusks, and the fact that many of their most prolific magic users slowly petrify with use of this magical power source is entirely unrelated, probably.

This daemonic essence powers vast forges, which have become the greatest engines of industry in the Mortal Realms. These create vast arsenals of weapons and constructs for the Helsmiths and their dubious allies, taint the land about them, and drive the forced evacuation of other local denizens like skaven, orruks, and Gloomspite Gitz.

The forge in Arkanaut is a recently repurposed duardin hold that the Helsmiths have claimed and desecrated (as they see it, they’ve just retaken a piece of their ancestral heritage and put it to use again). There are some great shots of the forge in this episode, inspired by the custom scenery created to accompany the recent Helsmiths of Hashut battletome.

There is one more power source at play in this episode, of course.

In episode 1, the Arkanauts harpooned themselves a Stormcast soul and trapped it inside a jury-rigged aether-tank, intending to sell it back to its brethren at a fair and reasonable price (or possibly another party at a less reasonable price, depending on market conditions).

Now the Helsmiths have the soul and we’re fairly sure they aren’t planning to use it for anything good…

Watch the full series of Arkanaut on Warhammer TV now, available as part of your Warhammer+ subscription.

item.title: Celebrate Warhammer Day with some suitably scary miniatures
item.description: Halloween and Warhammer are brought together in a list of some of our favourite terrifying models.
item.content:encoded:
Saturday is Warhammer Day! It’s also Halloween, so, to get ready we’re taking a look at some of our favourite terrifying Warhammer miniatures. 

Thousand Sons

Their whispered war cry is the last thing you’ll hear. These living suits of armour can’t be reasoned with, can’t be stopped, and they’re armed with magic guns!

Once proud Space Marines, Rubric Marines are now nothing more than a pile of dust and a corrupted soul, trapped inside a suit of power armour for all time, and commanded like a puppet by the arcane magic of warp-fuelled sorcerers. Some fates are worse than death.

Blood Angels

What would Halloween be without vampires? Blood Angels may not dislike garlic, but they are incredibly stylish, and do crave the taste of blood. Just remember, Space Marines have two hearts, so you’d better bring two stakes!

Blood Angels have a second flaw – the Black Rage – and none have ever truly been able to overcome it. That was until Mephiston, Chief Librarian of the Blood Angels, crossed the Rubicon Primaris and seemingly left his curse behind him. Don’t think he won’t nibble your neck though.

Necrons

While they may look skeletal, there’s no organic matter to be found on a Necron Warrior. These deathless automatons march without fear or mercy in eerie lockstep with a single-minded desire to destroy every living creature in the galaxy. You may be faster, but they’ll chase you forever.

Necron Warriors form the undead legions of the dynasties, and if it wasn’t scary enough staring into their dead, soulless eyes, then their guns can flay the flesh from any living creature. On top of that, one of their star gods was death incarnate, and is said to be the inspiration for the grim reaper.

Nighthaunt

The Nighthaunt are no mere ghosts, they are bitter, ethereal spirits that inflict terror, and drag down the souls of the living. Not to put too fine a point on it, these are not kids wearing bedsheets with eyeholes cut into them.

No figure in the worlds of Warhammer embodies the misery of the restless undead more than Lady Olynder, Mortarch of Grief. She is despair made manifest, gloom given form, and mortals in her presence are overwhelmed by a dread so potent that it can silence the heartbeat of even the strongest opponent. 

Gloomspite Gitz

While the motley assortment of creatures that make up the Gloomspite Gitz may seem “fun” to the casual observer, make no mistake, Squigs have very sharp teeth. And a lot of them. 

When grots take to the battlefield with a horde of Squigs, woe betide anyone who underestimates these vicious creatures. Little more than mouths with legs and a terrible appetite, Squigs are feared across the Mortal Realms, able to tear even the mightiest foe to shreds in a crimson blur.

Space Wolves

The full moon shines down through the inky black darkness. Out on the moor, you hear a blood-curdling howl. Wulfen are part Space Marine and part wolf, and they are probably the closest thing to a werewolf in the 41st Millennium.

Wulfen are bestial warriors, altered by the curse lying in the gene-seed of all scions of the Wolf King – hunters that bound forward with fangs bared and claws outstretched. They’re fast, and they hit hard with claws, teeth, and a variety of deadly weapons.

Join us in-store to celebrate Warhammer Day and Halloween! You’ll be able to pick up other scary models, such as skeletons, zombies, and other undead warriors. Plus, you can get Oath Fulfilled, the special commemorative miniature, who, if she gets sufficiently blessed by the Dark Gods, might make it onto this list for next year.

item.content:encoded:
It’s Warhammer Day on Saturday, and it’s not just about celebrating our own miniatures – there are also sales and reveals for a world of video games, merch, and more on the cards.

GOG | Gamesplanet | 
Fanatical | GamersGate  | Green Man Gaming

Warhammer Age of Sigmar: Deathmaster

Can't see this video?

This video is hosted on a third party website, which may be using cookies. To see it, you need to accept cookies by clicking on the button below. You can change your preferences at any time by clicking Cookie Settings at the bottom of any Warhammer Community page.

The delightfully devious stealth platformer Deathmaster has its story trailer revealed today. The story centers around Vinheek, a powerless Skaven prisoner when we first meet him, who has plans for greatness. Vihneek is freed by Skiteek, a fellow assassin from Clan Skrell – but Vihneek’s savior is ultimately his new captor. Clan Skrell wields Vihneek as a weapon, forcing him to complete deadly contracts at all costs and with no mercy. Every target Vihneek kills propels him higher within the Clan Skrell’s ranks, but looming threats from rival clans swirl…

Deathmaster is coming to Steam, XBOX Series S|X, PlayStation 5, and Nintendo Switch 2 in 2027, so get your knives sharpened and prepare to claw your way to the top of the Eshin hierarchy.

Warhammer 40,000: Battlesector

Battlesector turns 5 this year and to celebrate, a free update is landing on Warhammer Day adding a new map, gameplay options, and a major rebalance of units across the game. XBOX Play Anywhere also goes live today.

The next big DLC, Courage and Catastrophe, is also coming on 14 December, adding a 13-mission story campaign and three new units into the oodles of content already available.

item.title: The Warhammer 40,000 Updates Update
item.description: A Warhammer 40,000 rules log is incoming.
item.content:encoded:
You may have noticed that the October rules update for Warhammer 40,000 didn’t appear in your app as a single smooth release. Instead, it arrived as sporadic downloads over several days.

This is our bad.

We’re sorry for any confusion this caused. We’re going to do better. Here’s Adam to explain further:

Can't see this video?

This video is hosted on a third party website, which may be using cookies. To see it, you need to accept cookies by clicking on the button below. You can change your preferences at any time by clicking Cookie Settings at the bottom of any Warhammer Community page.

New Rules Update Log – coming with the next update

As Adam said in the video above, alongside the next version of the Warhammer 40,000 app, Warhammer Community is going to host a Rules Update Log to help explain the changes in simple terms. This log will list a summary of any rules changes along with date stamps to make it easy to track, which we hope will be particularly useful if you don’t play super regularly, and want to get caught up.

The next rules change for Warhammer 40,000 will be the quarterly balance update, set to be published the week beginning 7 December.

As a reminder, our aim with the cadence for any rules updates is that they be no more than monthly, with most changes limited to clarifications and addressing errors, and any more impactful amends limited to the quarterly balance updates. So unless your army gets a new Codex, you should really only need to check in four times a year for changes that make a substantive difference to your games.

item.title: Designers’ notes: Crafting the new House Orlock miniatures
item.description: The Necromunda team talks about creating the new models.
item.content:encoded:
A range of new Orlock miniatures for Necromunda are available for pre-order from Saturday. We sat down with the miniatures design team who created them to learn more about the new House of Iron Fighters.

Necromunda Design Team: When we started to work on the Orlock kits, we realised there was an opportunity to reinforce the grease monkey/biker theme that was developed after the release of Necromunda in 2017. We aimed to do this through giving them their own flavour, something that we felt had always been a bit underplayed with the Orlock. They carry tools, chains and any oil rags they may need to get the job done.

Let’s take a look at the new kits.

Road Sergeants and Road Warriors

The Road Sergeants & Cyber-Mastiffs kit is packed with options for your leaders and champions. It includes spud-jackers, grenade launchers, maces, scrap shields, a partial servo-harness with a harpoon launcher and a full servo-harness with servo-claws. There are also a pair of Cyber-Mastiffs! The Road Warriors expand your gang with different archetypes, opening up fresh tactics, and even add new weapons such as servo shotguns and scrap welders.

Necromunda Design Team: These kits were our chance to show a larger diversity of anatomies and gender – from the young Orlock Greenhorn who wants to prove themselves to the powerful and hardened Road Captains, and of course their loyal Cyber-Mastiffs!

Weapons-wise, we had some fun playing more with the Servo-harnesses, originally introduced with the Arms Masters, and offering a wider range of use for them, for example with the new ‘dirtnap servo-claws’, or the Road Shooter’s ‘servo-shotgun’ – and by doing so, pushing visually that they are skilled mechanics, some of them carrying actual V-twin-inspired engines on their back.

Ogryn Minders

Ogryns are some of the most frequently seen abhumans in the 41st Millennium. We’ve seen Servitor Ogryns in Necromunda before, but the new Minders have a distinctively Orlock flavour. The kit is packed with wargear options, including a maul, spud-jacker, knuckledusters, and ripper guns.

Necromunda Design Team: Another kit we had the chance to work on was the Ogryn Minder kit, introducing a new Ogryn to the Necromunda range. We ensured that we stayed true to the classic abhuman legacy – you could totally imagine this Ogryn being a retired Astra Militarum veteran hired by the gang to become a moody bouncer equipped with his good old ripper gun and wearing his handmade Orlock jacket. We gave them a variety of accessories and poses so they’re easy to customise, making them a must-have companion for any feared Road Captain.

Thanks, folks! The new Orlock miniatures are available to pre-order from Saturday, along with their Underhive Journal. If you’re brand new to the House of Iron, the Orlock Underhive Crew is a great way to start a gang.

item.title: Sequel to The Lords of Silence revealed
item.description: A new Warhammer 40,000 Death Guard novel is on the way from Black Library.
item.content:encoded:
Realm of Silence is the follow-up to the fan-favourite Death Guard tale, The Lords of Silence, by Chris Wraight. It picks up the story after the warriors of Nurgle have conquered the ancient Adeptus Astartes fortress world of Sabatine and its outlying planets.

The Lords of Silence, led by the savage Siegemaster Vorx, have established a new plague kingdom, dedicated to the glory of Nurgle. However, peace and stability rarely last for long in the grim darkness of the far future, and the Death Guard are not as united as they may have hoped. Soon, new enemies begin to circle, drawn by the enclave’s apparent vulnerability.

It’s not just external forces that threaten the Plague God’s newest dominion. Within its borders, old resentments simmer, as Vorx’s desire to create a kingdom of his own clashes with his second-in-command Dragan’s thirst to take the fight to the wider Imperium. Now it remains to be seen if the fragile Realm of Silence can survive the growing threats from both inside and out, or if the gathering tides of endless war will sweep it away as quickly as it was formed.

This new novel will be available as a regular hardback and a handsome Special Edition, which features an antiqued-brass effect metal medallion on the cover, gold page edges, and a new afterword by Chris Wraight.

The Lords of Silence is also getting a re-release in hardback so that it matches Realm of Silence and Grandfather Nurgle can start claiming your bookshelf.

Alongside Realm of Silence and The Lords of Silence, you’ll also be able to pick up some other Nurgle-themed treats. There’s a cotton tapestry measuring 80cm by 30cm, featuring artwork of Siegemaster Vorx in his plague kingdom, and a faux leather notebook, covered with images of bloatflies, to fill with your heretical writings.*

The release date for these tomes isn’t far away so keep your eyes on Warhammer Community to find out when you can add these delightfully disgusting novels to your own collection.

* Or army lists, notes for your next game, painting recipes…

item.title: On Warhammer+ this week – Storm Dragons and Slayer Swords
item.description: A look at the upcoming action this week on Warhammer TV.
item.content:encoded:
This week on Warhammer TV, Arkanaut concludes with a thunderous finale, forces clash in the heart of the World of Legend and you can catch up with loads of coverage from Golden Demon at SPIEL.

Available Today: Battle Report – Tomb Kings of Khemri vs Grand Cathay

What would have happened if Miao Ying, the Storm Dragon herself, had been blown off course on her way to Marienburg?* Find out in this week’s special four-player Warhammer: The Old World Battle Report. Can the might of Grand Cathay overcome the necromantic horror of King Iratekh the Hallowed and his Tomb Kings of Khemri?

You’ll just have to watch to find out! Even better, you can try out the scenario yourself, with bonus points for claiming the tomb and slaying (or surviving) Wizards – download it for free now:

Download Now

We sat down with Battle Report host Si to learn a bit more about the scenario, and this week’s epic clash.

Si: To celebrate our long-awaited return to the Old World on Battle Report this week, we decided to go a bit crazy with it! First of all, it’s a doubles game with a twist, in that both sides divided up a single 2,000-point army between them instead of each player bringing along 1,000 points. That way, Rhu and I could more easily indulge in a powerful character such as Miao Ying to lead our army of Grand Cathay, while having a single, powerful Hierophant on the Tomb Kings side offered Dan and David a bigger risk and reward. Speaking of Dave, he was even kind enough to design us a custom narrative scenario to play, which, through the arcane powers of the internet, you can play at home too!

This scenario turned out to be a fascinating tactical challenge for Rhu and I on the Cathayan side. On one hand, we could attempt a belligerent sledgehammer attack down the middle of the battlefield – the most direct path towards the tomb.** That said, this would risk us getting bogged down and eventually overwhelmed by the massed Tomb Kings infantry, who could, of course, magically replenish their numbers. On the other hand, we could try to hold the centre and make a big hook around one of the flanks, or maybe even attempt a pincer movement around both. In the end, we went for a bit of a mix of all three! Make sure you check out the episode to see how we got on.

Thanks, Si! Watch the episode now to see which army came out on top.

Through the Week: Painting Desk Roadshow – Golden Demon at SPIEL

The Painting Desk Roadshow team packed up their brushes and headed to SPIEL at the weekend. Throughout the week, you’ll be able to watch their interviews with some top painters, including Angelo Di Chello, Maxime Penaud, Simon Sikora, Luke Wiggering, and a second, very special chat with Maxime Penaud who won the coveted Slayer Sword. 

Available Now: Loremasters – Khazalite Holds

Across the Mortal Realms, mountain keeps once long-abandoned now echo to the sound of awakened forges, grumbled oaths, and prayers to the Ancestor Gods. The duardin of the Khazalite Holds have returned to reclaim what is rightfully theirs.

Learn more about the newest faction in Warhammer Age of Sigmar. Presenter Alex delves into the karaks of the Kromdron, their military forces, and the pantheon of Ancestor Gods they revere. If you want to learn more about dour Gazul’s defence of the underworld or how Grungni forged his legendary alliance with Sigmar, this is the episode for you.

Available on Friday: Arkanaut – Episode 3: Dark Kindred

Episode three of animated series Arkanaut hits Warhammer TV this Friday, and things aren’t looking good for the crew of the Therodoson. We’ll have more details, including the official trailer and a behind-the-scenes look at the explosive series finale, on launch day.

This week’s features join a staggering back catalogue of over 700 episodes including original animations, hobby guides and gaming content. Remember, your subscription also unlocks a host of premium features in the Warhammer 40,000 and Age of Sigmar apps, not to mention access to Warhammer Vault and a treasure trove of lore books and articles large enough to make any duardin’s eyes bulge.

If you subscribe for an entire year, you’ll also gain automatic entry into regular competitions, a copy of the Warhammer Yearbook and even a pair of special subscriber-only miniatures. If that wasn’t enough, an annual subscription nets you 12 months of content for the price of nine.

item.title: Warhammer Age of Sigmar: October Update
item.description: Rules changes for Khazalite Holds, Sons of Behemat, and more.
item.content:encoded:
New rules updates are going live for Warhammer Age of Sigmar – read on to see if they affect your army.

Warhammer Age of Sigmar

Major changes: Khazalite Holds, Sons of Behemat

Minor changes: Ogor Mawtribes, Lumineth Realm-lords, Skaven, Sylvaneth, Nighthaunt

With the advent of new battletomes, a few older rules needed a quick update to stay relevant – namely where keywords were involved. The Khazalite Holds in particular see a lot of older FYRESLAYERS keywords turned into the new GRIMMDRON,* so things like the Fyreslayers Scourge of Aqshy rules can still be used.

As well as having their keywords changed, the Lofnir Drothkeepers Army of Renown has also been rewritten slightly to better fit their new rules. Notably, it now includes an additional way to generate grudge marks when your Magmadroths are killed.

The Sons of Behemat previously struggled to field game-legal 2,000 point Armies of Renown without needing to dip into Auxiliaries, so now they have a new option to field regiments led by Mancrusher Gargants.** This applies for both the Matriarch’s Mob and Stomper Tribe, so now’s a great time to give their new options a go.

Besides these two larger updates, a few fixes and clarifications have been added to several factions, such as the Skaven’s Verminlord Corruptor having its points corrected after a typo in the last update – one that most of you caught onto anyway, but a slip-up nonetheless! Some units like Pyregheists and Ydrilan Riverblades can also now double up their Champions when reinforced, like other, similar warscrolls. If your faction of choice is listed under minor changes, have a quick look for their updates with the New tag (or search for the ✹ icon).

Spearhead

Major changes: None

Minor changes: Daughters of Khaine Heartflayer Troupe, Nighthaunt Slasher Host, Orruk Warclans Swampskulka Gang, Seraphon Sunblood Prowlers

This is one of the largest Spearhead updates we’ve had for a while, with a handful of ability clarifications that add the ‘Once Per Turn (Army)’ condition to bring them in line with other factions. Otherwise, it’s business as usual in the Spearhead arena, so get out into the City of Ash and show those scuttling Skaven miscreants what for.

Download the latest changes, enjoy your battles in the Mortal Realms, and if you have anything you need answered, make sure to send your questions to AoSFAQ@gwplc.com.

Download now

* Rules Update PDF page 33.
** Rules Update PDF page 72.

item.title: Maxime Penaud talks about winning the Slayer Sword
item.description: A closer look at the stunning miniature and a chat with the winning painter.
item.content:encoded:
On Sunday, Maxime Penaud lifted his third Slayer Sword. Let’s take a closer look at the incredible miniature that triumphed at the European leg of Golden Demon 2026.

Can't see this video?

This video is hosted on a third party website, which may be using cookies. To see it, you need to accept cookies by clicking on the button below. You can change your preferences at any time by clicking Cookie Settings at the bottom of any Warhammer Community page.

Maxime took home the coveted sword at SPIEL in Germany last weekend for this amazing take on the legendary Ultramarines warrior, Marneus Calgar.

Speaking with Warhammer TV after his victory, Maxime spoke about his first encounter with the ultimate Warhammer painting competition, “Golden Demon is really special to me, I discovered Golden Demon when I was 12 – I remember looking at all the winners in White Dwarf.”

Having entered a Death Guard miniature in 2023, Maxime chatted about the different challenge presented by the Ultramarines Chapter Master, “I decided to choose a model that is that clean, this way I wasn’t able to hide anything – you have to paint everything perfect.”

Finally, Maxime discussed how much he enjoys Golden Demon as a whole, “for me, it’s magic to see all these painters from all around the world.”

This is Maxime’s third Slayer Sword, having also won at Warhammer Fest in 2019 and at Games Day France in 2010. He also won gold Golden Demons at Warhammer World in 2022 and at Warhammer Fest in 2023.

You’ll be able to watch a more in-depth interview with Maxime as part of the Painting Desk Roadshow on Warhammer TV today where he talks about how he painted Marneus Calgar. Then, come back tomorrow to hear him chatting about winning the Slayer Sword. 

Painting Desk Roadshow features interviews with top painters from SPIEL all week. Subscribe now and enjoy all five episodes as they are released.

item.title: Warhammer Day – Chaos Champions through the ages
item.description: Take a look back at the heroes of the Dark Gods over the years.
item.content:encoded:
Warhammer Day is this Saturday, and this year’s celebratory miniature – available in stores this weekend – is a majestic Darkoath Warqueen from the Mortal Realms, her Oath Fulfilled. 

This stunning new depiction of a mortal champion of Chaos made some of the… shall we say more seasoned members of the team misty-eyed with nostalgia, so we decided to take a wander down the eightfold path of memory lane and look at Chaos Champions of bygone ages.

Chaos was present from the very beginning of Warhammer Fantasy Battles in 1983, but it was the 1990s that ushered in a plethora of new Champion models directly themed to each of the gods. This was the start of an iterative process that led to the distinct Chaos factions that exist now in the Age of Sigmar. Over the years, the style of each god’s followers was refined across multiple editions and releases, to where we are now.*

Khorne

Nurgle

Slaanesh

Tzeentch

Chaos Undivided

Of course, not all mortal followers of Chaos worship one specific god. Many of them are into Chaos in all its undivided glory,** and the aesthetic of these Champions has also evolved, with both Warhammer: The Old World and Warhammer Age of Sigmar bringing their own twists to the formula in recent years.

The Everchosen

We would be remiss not to mention the greatest Warhammer champion of them all – Archaon. He and his trusty mount Dorghar have experienced their own evolution that echoes that of the wider Chaos faction. 

Darkoath

Warhammer Age of Sigmar, as well as allowing for more detailed explorations of the god-dedicated forces, also opened up space to expand on the Marauders archetype, turning them from a couple of units that followed in the wake of their armoured pals to a fully fleshed-out subfaction of chieftains and Warqueens… which brings us back to Oath Fulfilled. 

Head to your local Warhammer store this Saturday, 31 October, to join in the Warhammer Day celebrations and pick up your very own Oath Fulfilled – with all those textures, we reckon she’s the perfect miniature to try the new Warhammer Tone Pro range on. 

store finder

Find your store

* Okay, not all of these specific aesthetics have survived – sorry, big hand guy.

** And who can blame them? Some days you want blood and skulls, and others you just fancy a change…

item.title: New battleforce boxes revealed for Warhammer Age of Sigmar
item.description: Start a new collection or expand your existing army.
item.content:encoded:
We’ve seen this year’s crop of Warhammer 40,000 battleforce boxes, and now it’s time to reveal the ones for Warhammer Age of Sigmar.

Stormcast Eternals: Annihilation Host

  • Lord-Commander Bastian Carthalos

  • Lord-Relictor

  • Lord-Celestant

  • 3 Praetors

  • 6 Annihilators

  • 3 Annihilators with Meteoric Grandhammers

Crush Sigmar’s enemies with an unstoppable force of heavy Stormcast infantry, led by the peerless Lord-Commander Bastian Carthalos. Your opponents will know what hit them, and it’ll be a bunch of devastating (war)hammers.

Cities of Sigmar: Knights of Hammerhal

  • Tahlia Vedra, Lioness of the Parch

  • Freeguild Cavalier-Marshal

  • 10 Freeguild Cavaliers

Tahlia Vedra leads a powerful cavalry charge through the gates of your Castelite formation, flanked by the thundering hooves of the Freeguild Cavaliers. They’re speed, power, and style all in one package – perfect for the centrepiece to a wider army.

Maggotkin of Nurgle: Plaguesworn Host

  • Harbinger of Decay

  • Lord of Blights

  • 3 Sloven Knights

  • 5 Putrid Blightkings

  • 10 Rotswords

  • 14 Pox-Wretches

  • 6 Mire Kelpies

Muster a diverse and potent force of Nurgle’s finest plague-bringers with the Plaguesworn Host, which includes a healthy* mix of tough champions, swarming creatures, and mobile cavalry. It’s a solid core around which you can expand a greater Maggotkin of Nurgle army, be it with daemons, larger monsters, or even more resilient infantry.

Orruk Warclans: Grunta Stampede

  • Tuskboss on Maw-Grunta (can alternatively be built as Maw-Grunta Gouger or Maw-Grunta with Hakkin' Krew)

  • Maw-Grunta Gouger (can alternatively be built as Tuskboss on Maw-Grunta or Maw-Grunta with Hakkin' Krew)

  • 6 Gore-Gruntas

Ironjaw Orruks are difficult to stop at the best of times, and become downright wrecking balls when mounted on the back of ornery beasts known as gruntas.** Two big ‘uns riding larger Maw-Gruntas are your hammers, with the (relatively) smaller gore-grunta cavalry stampeding in their wake.

Nighthaunt: Court of the Undying King

  • Nagash, Supreme Lord of the Undead

  • 2 Dreadblade Harrows

  • 10 Dreadscythe Harridans

  • 10 Bladegheist Revenants

  • 10 Grimghast Reapers

Every soul in the Mortal Realms belongs to the Great Necromancer by right, and if the living need convincing of this inalienable fact, the Court of the Undying King will demonstrate it at the end of a spectral blade. Such is the power of Nagash!

Slaves to Darkness: Legion of Damnation

  • Chaos Lord on Daemonic Mount

  • 5 Chaos Chosen

  • 3 Varanguard

  • 5 Chaos Knights

  • 10 Chaos Warriors

The armoured legions of the Varanspire march on the lands of Order, Death, and Destruction, led by a fierce-eyed Chaos Lord. This elite warband is the equal of any force in the Mortal Realms, and wouldn’t dare disappoint the Grand Marshal of the Apocalypse, so you’re in safe hands.

These battleforce boxes will be available for pre-order soon, so keep an eye out for their arrival in our Sunday Preview articles over the next few weeks to learn exactly when. They’re a great starting point for a new foray into the Mortal Realms, and make an excellent gift for the truly special Warhammer fans in your life.***

* For a given value of ‘healthy’ – this is Nurgle after all.
** Or ‘big pigs’ as they’re affectionately known in the Warhammer Community office.
*** Or even as a present for yourself!

item.title: Huge Warhammer 40,000: Dawn of War IV game overview trailer revealed
item.description: Discover the factions, missions, maps, and more for the video game.
item.content:encoded:
We’re just weeks away from the release of Warhammer 40,000: Dawn of War IV. Prepare for your return to Kronos with an epic, nine-minute trailer:

Can't see this video?

This video is hosted on a third party website, which may be using cookies. To see it, you need to accept cookies by clicking on the button below. You can change your preferences at any time by clicking Cookie Settings at the bottom of any Warhammer Community page.

In the fourth installment of the legendary Warhammer 40,000 real-time strategy game series, you can take control of four factions – the Space Marines of the Blood Ravens and Dark Angels, Orks, Necrons, and Adeptus Mechanicus – across four campaigns comprising more than 70 thrilling missions.


In addition to the campaigns, there’s a Skirmish mode, with dozens of customisable settings, four game types, and support for up to five AI opponents, where you can hone your skills before taking the battle online across 30 multiplayer maps.

The Last Stand

Fan-favourite co-op survival mode The Last Stand is back, where you and two allies must hold the line against relentless waves of enemies. Choose from five heroes and assemble your strike force of companion units, bringing new layers of strategic depth to every run.

Whichever mode you like to play, the enhanced Painter tool means you can make every army your own. Choose from dozens of presets or create your own schemes with choices of colours, decals, and wargear – for the first time, you have complete creative control to paint your units’ armour and equipment piece-by-piece.

Warhammer 40,000: Dawn of War IV is due for release on 3 December 2026, but if you can’t wait until then, the Commander Edition gives players early access three days ahead of the main release. Pre-order either edition now to get a 10% discount, and prepare to begin the fight for Kronus anew.

item.title: New Battleforce boxes revealed for Warhammer 40,000
item.description: Easily start a new army or grow an existing one.
item.content:encoded:
Christmas is quickly approaching – see what Warhammer 40,000 Battleforce boxes you’ll be able to pick up this festive season.

Space Marines: Indomitus Task Force

  • Captain In Terminator Armour

  • Chaplain

  • Redemptor Dreadnought

  • 5 Terminators 

  • 5 Assault Intercessors with Jump Packs

  • 10 Intercessors

The Indomitus Task Force gives you a versatile core to base a Space Marines army around, and includes a little bit of everything Warhammer armies need – shooting, fighting, and durability.

Chaos Knights: Helhunt Lance

  • Knight Ruinator (can alternatively be built as Knight Abominant, Knight Rampager, or Knight Desecrator)

  • 4 War Dog Stalkers (can alternatively be built as War Dog Brigands or War Dog Karnivores)

Dominate the battlefield by sending your tough and terrifying Chaos Knight up the middle of the battlefield while nimble War Dogs snap at the flanks. Just make sure to protect your big guy, and you’ll be stomping corpse-worshippers in no time.

Orks: Armoured Blitzmob

  • Warboss In Mega Armour

  • Battlewagon (can alternatively be built as a Gunwagon)

  • Deff Dread 

  • 3 Meganobz

  • 10 Ork Boyz

Load your Meganobz and Warboss into a Gunwagon and blast them up the field in double-quick time, before unloading everything into your opponent’s face at point-blank range. Build it as a Battlewagon, and you can even fit all 10 of the Boyz in at the same time.

Space Wolves: Champions of Fenris

  • Logan Grimnar

  • Arjac Rockfist

  • 15 Wolf Guard Terminators

Unleash Fenris’ finest with a mass of powerful Wolf Guard Terminators, led by the Great Wolf himself and his personal champion. It’s a force as blunt and savage as the Space Wolves themselves, and a terrifying prospect for any enemy.

Blood Angels: Angelus Assault Force

  • Commander Dante 

  • Blood Angels Chaplain with Jump Pack

  • Death Company Brutalis Dreadnought

  • 3 Sanguinary Guard

  • 5 Death Company Marines with Jump Packs

  • Blood Angels Upgrade Frame

The Blood Angels love a thunderous flight into the thick of the melee, and the Angelus Assault Force gives you units you need to crash down on your foes. All of your infantry hurtle in from above, while the enemy is rightly distracted by a rampaging Brutalis Dreadnought rapidly charging towards them.

Chaos Space Marines: Cult of Destruction

  • Warpsmith

  • Defiler

  • Venomcrawler

  • 2 Obliterators

  • 5 Havocs

  • 3 Mutilators

Heavy weapons and hulking daemon engines are a particular favourite of the Iron Warriors, but you can use this Battleforce to represent any Chaos warband. After all, who in their right mind would turn down a Defiler, especially one flanked by some of the toughest and deadliest infantry this side of the Great Rift?

Necrons: Disciples of the Nekrosor

  • C'tan Shard of the Nightbringer

  • Nekrosor Ammentar

  • 3 Ophydian Destroyers

  • Canoptek Doomstalker

  • 10 Necron Warriors

  • 3 Canoptek Scarab Swarms

Nekrosor Ammentar and his collection of Nightbringer C’tan Shards made an incredible mess around Ultramar and now have their sights set on the rest of the galaxy. Two powerful centrepiece miniatures surrounded by some Necrons mainstays is ideal for reclaiming your lost empire.

If you fancy picking up one of these Battleforce boxes for yourself, or as a Christmas gift for your Warhammer-inclined friends or family, they’ll be available for pre-order soon. Keep checking in with us to be the first to learn exactly when. And stay tuned to find out what’s on offer for Warhammer Age of Sigmar and Warhammer: The Horus Heresy.

item.title: Da Red Gobbo returns with a new festive miniature
item.description: Plus, there’s a new novel starring the galaxy’s greatest revolutionary gretchin.
item.content:encoded:
Da Red Gobbo is back with another festive miniature – and this time he’s got himself a Squigmobile. Just make sure you’re out of the way – we’re not convinced he knows how to stop!

Da Red Gobbo’s Squigmobile is a roaring, clanking contraption geared towards delivering presents at exceptionally high speed, which we dare say channels more than a few Wazdakka Gutsmek vibes. His long-suffering ‘elf’ assistant looks frankly miserable in the bomb-shaped sidecar – which honestly might just be a live bomb – but knowing what a jolly fellow Da Red Gobbo can be, he’s probably overreacting.

See, da Gobbo is a safety-conscious boss. He’s even wearing a helmet.*

This miniature will be available to pre-order soon, and if you want to use it in some fun casual games, make sure to grab this year’s Festive Activities Guide from your local Warhammer store in November. It contains Legends rules for Warhammer 40,000, Nemesis Operatives rules for Kill Team, and as unlikely as it sounds, Blood Bowl rules.

Alongside the Squigmobile, our favourite yuletide revolutionary stars in a brand-new novella from Chem Dog author Callum Davis – Da Red Gobbo’s Reckoning.

This raucous tale revolves around the ratling fixer Ector Flynn and his squad of snipers, who are sent into a snow-cloaked wasteland by choleric Catachan commanders to hunt Da Red Gobbo down. After months of being bullied and knocked around by the Jungle Fighters, Flynn’s team welcome the chance to finally prove their worth, but nothing goes to plan when Da Gobbo is involved and they may come back learning a little something about vengeance from their red-coated quarry.

Keep an eye on Warhammer Community to find out when you can pick up the new miniature and book. In the meantime, catch up with the rest of Da Red Gobbo’s adventures with Long Live Da Red Gobbo, Da Gobbo’s Demise, Da Gobbo’s Revenge, and Da Gobbo Rides again – all available via the Black Library app.

* Health and safety isn’t just for the Iron Warriors.

item.title: Chronicles of Ruin – The Weight of Remembrance
item.description: Enjoy free fiction for the Khazalite Holds.
item.content:encoded:
The Khazalite Holds Army Set goes on pre-order tomorrow. Learn more about the new Warhammer Age of Sigmar faction with this free short story.

She crouched to listen to the stones, and through their vibrations, the stones spoke back.

‘The troggoths are in the western gallery, Thrynn,’ Helgur said, standing and brushing herself down. Over her head soared an archway of immaculate stone: the boundary mark of Karak Vigg. Beyond that was the tunnel ceiling, glimmering faintly, arcing down towards the half-finished gate into the hold behind them. ‘On the move now, as you might imagine.’

‘How long until they reach us?’ Thrynn Bjarki was a mountain of cave-bear fur, polished gromril and the accoutrements of various clans and guilds – a figure carved, as if by the Maker himself, into a monument to Khazalite culture. Amidst it all was a face and eyes that were stern but not quite unkind. Helgur shrugged, remaining just on the right side of respectful, as she dusted off her hands and glanced along the gloom-gripped passage before them.

‘With the luck of the Whitebeard? Still not long. Especially if the alpha-beast is among them. Likely before Kyng Vargrimm and his reinforcements arrive.’

‘Time enough to burn out any last nerves with a drink, though.’ The interjection was vigorous, lit with an undercurrent of flame. Helgur and Bjarki turned and watched as a wildly mohicaned warrior clad in drake pelt and gold approached from the duardin throng gathered at the hold’s entrance behind them.

Considering she had scowled through every war council and Great Recitation, Volna grinned now. It was an unusual expression on the scarred face of Urgma-Grimnir’s daughter; then again, it was unusual on the face of any Fyreslayer. Volna wore her battle-lust openly, though, three tankards of frothing magmalt ale drawn from the kegs the duardin had brought with them clutched in her broad hands.

‘One for you too, our worthy Stonesmith.’ The Fyreslayer thrust the sloshing mug at Helgur, downing a great swill of ale and wiping her mouth on the back of her hand.

‘I’m no Stonesmith, Runedaughter.’ Helgur took a drink, but her voice was terse. ‘I’m no less a fighter than you, as were all my line. I just… hear the stones.’

‘I hear them too, lass. You know what they tell me?’ Volna’s cinderous eyes flashed. ‘They talk of death. They talk about righting one more wrong. They talk of opening throats and splitting bellies and cleansing the rock with trogg blood. You know about that, lass? You know about vengeance?’

‘Aye,’ Helgur spat, reaching to the pendant around her neck. Her father’s sharp rune-work bumped beneath her finger, as it had many times since she had recovered it from what remained of his pulverised body. ‘Aye, I know about that.’

‘Enough, both of you. Defending the karak is what matters.’ Bjarki downed his own ale and gestured with his hammer back along the tunnel, to where pillars and half-built arches marked the edge of the Khazalites’ reconstruction efforts. ‘Grimnir would have our wrath saved for our enemies.’

‘See to your own duties, Thrynn. We’ll mind the Burning Berserker’s legacy.’ A harsh, gruff laugh left Volna as she raised her tankard in acknowledgement. A breath later and she turned, scale-cloak swirling, to march back to her glowering kin and grunting droth-beast at the eastern edge of the throng.

‘Strange folk, those Grimmdron slayers,’ Helgur said once she was gone, head shaking.

‘They might say the same of you, given how easily they bait you,’ Bjarki said, hammer braced over a shoulder. ‘I know you’re eager, lass. Just don’t lose sight of what we’re fighting for.’ 

‘Remembrance is strength. Through honouring what has been, we craft what is yet to be.’

‘Quoting my own words back at me, eh?’ Bjarki chuckled. He shook his head, beard swaying and clan-totems clinking. ‘Ah, niece. Your father was the same when we were lads, but he learned wisdom. We don’t put such stock in remembrance just to kindle hate. We remember to remind ourselves what is at stake.’ 

‘I know, lord-uncle,’ Helgur grunted, head bowed but not quite chastised. ‘But since it was this sort of beast that took him from us, some grudgement might be excused.’

‘Grudgement, aye. But grudgement must serve a purpose. Left untended, it digs to unhappy delves,’ Bjarki said, his tone suddenly severe. It did not last long before he sighed and clapped Helgur on the shoulder. 

‘Go on, girl. Greet your mother for me should you see her.’

Helgur set off at a steady jog, braids jostling. She passed ranks of duardin preparing for battle, acknowledging some with nods or grunts. Clans of axe and hammer compared the craftsmanship of their weapons; gunners sat carving resonant glyphs upon their ammunition; Runewrights performed final checks on the arcane mechanisms of great Oathkeeper guns. 

Amongst the war throng stood the Gholems. Each warrior-monolith seemed to possess its own gravity. The Gazulite Gholems, clutching their two-handed hammers, stood apart, the duardin who huddled around them chanting in low, morbid tones. Passing them, Helgur headed for the gleam of gold banding that marked the Valayan Gholems and the shield-maids clustered around them. 

‘How was your uncle?’ It was still odd, seeing Imnod clad as a templar of the hearth-goddess. That said, Helgur had always thought her mother had a severe aspect, and the tight mail coif and ceremonial hair buns had not diminished that impression. Perhaps that was why the matrons of Valaya’s guardian-shrine had recruited her. The will of the ancestors, they had said. That the summons came hours before they were due to have laid Helgur’s father to rest could not be helped.

‘Resolute, mother,’ Helgur said. ‘I expected more…’

‘Fire?’ Imnod asked, eyebrow arched. ‘Every battle is an echo of another. Through those echoes, we recall the virtue of those who fought them, so we might honour them.’

‘Words of the hearth-guardian?’

‘Of my own, girl!’ Imnod’s laughter was brief. Soon her face grew firm, and she gestured back along the torch-lit underway. ‘Beyond this gate lie our forges, our hearths, our folk. Now these beasts come to reduce all that to rubble. Steel and courage will cast them back.’

‘So folk keep telling me,’ Helgur nodded. ‘But I would rather honour Thorgrim and keep my grudge burning hot.’

A deep, bass gurgling echoed from further down the passage. As a hush fell over the throng, there came a wave of stench. Warriors jostled into position, shields locking. Imnod disappeared back into the ranks of her closed order. Helgur took position in the back ranks of her own warrior band just in time for someone to raise the cry.

‘Troggoths!’

The host of horribles shambled from the gloom, knuckles dragging and mauls carving furrows. They were accelerating. From amongst the Khazalite lines, light flashed and arcane energy left its peculiar odour as cannon-tenders struck the runes of activation, seeing their machines belch obliterating shot. Gunners joined the salvo, bullets whistling into eyes and soft flesh. Volna’s blazing slayers were already in motion; the right flank of the throng had charged to smash into the troggoth mob’s own, incinerating beast-flesh as they went. And all the while, the rest of the warrior throng clanged weapons against shields like great echoing gongs, stomped their feet and began to chant.

‘Clan Valankrom, who burned the gruel-beasts from the pits of Angaraz and made Ayadah safe anew, we remember your courage!’

‘The clans of Hasgaard, who honoured Grimnir and stood firm against the hordes of the Troggoth King, we remember your ferocity!’

‘Valaya the Defender, who broke the Gargant’s Gate and saved the clans of Karak Mogram, we remember your fortitude!’

‘And we remember those murdered by beasts,’ Helgur murmured quietly, reaching up to her father’s charm, ‘in whose name I will slay a hundred.’

Many troggoths had been engaged by the Fyreslayers; as sparks flew from gold-inlaid weapons, Helgur saw Volna’s Magmadroth rear up and let loose a blazing flame-stream at the mammoth brute grappling with it. But the rest of the beasts remained a juddering avalanche, and now they hit home. The first rank of duardin were knocked sprawling by their momentum. Not so the second. At Bjarki’s bellowed insistence, they gritted teeth, dug in heels, bent backs and pushed. They strode back against the troggoths even as the dull beasts grunted, baffled at why these little things were not simply breaking. They cleaved bellies or pinned beasts in place as firepower ripped through them. 

Imnod’s henge of Valayans was with them, drawing the enemy’s rage onto themselves while their long halberds speared and sliced. Helgur, along with the other reserve warriors, was preparing to join the scrum when an unhealthy groaning echoed off the tunnel wall beside them. In that pain was a warning, one that raked along Helgur’s spine.

‘The alpha-beast,’ she whispered as she fruitlessly scanned the fighting. ‘Inghilde’s lantern, where’s the alpha?’ 

There was an explosion of stone, a rush of force. Helgur was knocked from her feet as masonry and rock spun; it was this that saved her, her kin instead pulped into smears. As she blinked through the grit-haze, the sight of something monstrous shouldering through the destruction saw her spit a curse. The troggoth chief’s body seethed with motion: scuttling creatures of the deep and dark. In each hand, it carried half of an immense ancestor statue ground down into a club. 

Helgur doubted it had meant to punch through as part of some coordinated flank attack. Likely it had just wandered into a different tunnel and heard the sound of their chanting on the other side of the wall. Those beady yellow eyes locked upon her. She reached for her father’s charm, hoping to draw some measure of fury from it. Her fingers found the rune etched there. It was then, only then, that she recognised the pattern.

In her grief, in her grudgement, Helgur had not looked too closely at the actual design. She had presumed it was a weapon-rune. It was not; it was galaz. ‘Precious’. 

The beast looked along the duardin passageway, drawn towards the reclaimed works of the Khazalites by the light. Few save Helgur stood in its path of demolition. And, to her own surprise, that realisation burned through thoughts of vengeance.

‘I remember you, father,’ Helgur whispered. ‘I remember what you died for. Remember me as I die for it too.’

Getting to her feet, she moved to charge. The troggoth bellowed, raising a makeshift bludgeon. It swung, and her world went black – because she had closed her eyes. But the eternal darkness that should have followed did not. Instead came the resonant clang of weapon against shield. 

The orestone at the heart of each of the Valayan Gholems glowed with pulsing blue light as they stomped between Helgur and the marauding titan. Furious at being denied an easy meal, the troggoth set its shoulders and barged into them. One toppled, still swinging as it fell. The rest stood firm as the deep and resonant songs of Imnod’s henge of warriors flowed over the melee. The Gholems bashed the beast with their shields, splitting its lumpen nose. One hacked off an ear before having its own head annihilated with a wild swing.

A spinning shard of stone cut open Helgur’s cheek, seeing her flinch. The Gholems, for all their heroism, were being broken open. But they had bought seconds – crucial, unbending seconds. Seconds enough for a horn-blast to ring and the torches back down the underway passage to glow bright. Feet stamped and shields clanged to the echo of chanting, this time with force enough to shake the mountain.

Even as the Gholems battered it, the troggoth turned, brow furrowed – just as a spear of hexagonal rock burst from the earth and punched through its gut like an ore-pressing piston. The beast howled, dazed, as something equally huge sailed along an undulating current of rock towards it. Surrounded now by the Gholems, Helgur joined the cheers as the throne-barge of Kyng Vargrimm crashed forth, the duardin lord slicing through the troggoth’s neck with one punishing axe-swing. 

Warriors parted before him as the Kyng rode into the fray, the broken stone left by the troggoth’s entrance curving like a tube-wave at the chanting of Vargrimm’s Stonesmiths. Lightning spat from the drake-headed prows of his vessel, adding their firepower to the roaring barrage the Oathkeepers fired in his honour. Fresh clan warriors marched behind him, banners flashing with the sigils of the hold. Even some of Volna’s kin came with them, magmic veins of power threading along muscles as they sang ur-songs of awakening and doom.

Whatever intellect the troggoths possessed was not enough to see them retreat in time. Little by little, the duardin spilled over them, and their weapon arms did not tire. Helgur saw Imnod atop a felled brute, expression unbending as she stabbed down into its gaping mouth while shielding a wounded clan warrior with her body. Panicked, heavy breaths finally escaped Helgur’s chest. She allowed herself to sit as her heart slowed its hammering. One hand still clutched her amulet. 

‘I did not slay a single one, father. Not a single one.’ As she spoke, Helgur felt herself smile. Her body slumped against the leg of a Gholem, the stone warrior having now returned to a motionless docility. She glanced back along the underway. The torches burned bright. The pillars remained uncracked. The artifice of the duardin was unmarred. And where there was artifice, there was life. That, at least, was what the stones said to her now.

‘But I remembered. Remembered that vengeance isn’t everything. That we’re here to build, not just to slay. Perhaps that’s a good start, aye?’

The Khazalite Holds launch their campaign to reclaim their former empire tomorrow when their new army set goes on pre-order. In the meantime, enjoy some free Fyreslayers fiction as you prepare to unleash the  Grimmdrom alongside the Kromdron.

item.title: Khazalite Holds Clanshields Kit Focus
item.description: Get a closer look at the new duardin miniatures for Warhammer Age of Sigmar.
item.content:encoded:
The new Khazalite Holds Clanshields kit is packed with awesome build options, making it simple to customise your unit. Take a look at just how many ways you can put together the miniatures.

The 10 miniatures come with interchangeable shields – 10 with one rune so you can have a unified look, and the other 10 with different runes to mix it up.

The heads are also interchangeable and there are enough with beards that you can give them all a hirsute appearance if you like. 

Each Clanshield can be armed with a hammer or an axe – they have the same in-game profile as each other, and if the Kromdron can’t pick a favourite then you shouldn’t have to either.

The kit also includes parts to build an optional champion, standard bearer, and musician, all with more cosmetic options. The champion has a choice of two tactical rocks and three icon plates that they share with the standard bearer. Speaking of your banner waver, they have a choice of two standards, each with a choice of toppers, while the musician can choose from two different warhorns.

As well as being an incredibly flexible kit, the Clanshields are the backbone of Khazalite Holds armies. Their 3+ save makes them resilient and they get to add 1 to their wound rolls when they have any grudge marks.

As one, these duardin recite the names of their fallen clanfolk and are instilled with a determination that their loss will not be in vain.

Effect: Add 1 to wound rolls for this unit’s attacks while it has any grudge marks.

These new miniatures will be available for the first time in the Khazalite Holds Army Set, which is available for pre-order from Saturday. The army set makes a complete Spearhead – Drakkblud’s Clanguard.

Led by Hjulda Drakkblud, the Clanshields are supported by an Oathkeeper Cannon – firing stone-carved ammunition – and three Gholems of Gazul, who can each have different runes on their hammers.

The Oathkeeper Cannon can alternatively be built as a Stonebreaker Mortar, and the Gholems of Gazul can alternatively be built as Gholems of Valaya. These additional build options aren’t included in the Spearhead assembly guide in the army set, but you can download for free now:

Download now

item.title: Only in Death: 40,000 Ways to Die – New Animation
item.content:encoded:
It might sound great to be a genetically enhanced superhuman killing machine, but the life of a Space Marine is far from sunshine and roses. In fact, what you thought was sunshine is just as likely to be the flash of an Aeldari starcannon 0.1 seconds before it utterly vaporises you.

With their new Codex on the way, we thought it high time we took a look at the reality of life as a Space Marine in the 41st Millennium, through the medium of endearing cartoon-animated Intercessors being mercilessly dismembered.

Enjoy!

It’s a great time to start a Space Marines army – the new Codex is available to pre-order now, alongside a raft of new kits. Forge your force, and lead the Emperor’s finest into battle (and probably death) today.
